requirements.quote: Unidirectional streams carry data in one direction: from the initiator of the stream to its peer.
requirements.condition: When carrying data on a unidirectional stream
requirements.required_behavior: Permit data flow only from the stream initiator to its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not permit data flow from the peer back to the stream initiator.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can attempt data transfer in each direction on a unidirectional stream and verify the permitted direction.

requirements.quote: Bidirectional streams allow for data to be sent in both directions.
requirements.condition: When carrying data on a bidirectional stream
requirements.required_behavior: Permit data to be sent in both directions.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that each endpoint can send data on the same bidirectional stream.

requirements.quote: Streams are identified within a connection by a numeric value, referred to as the stream ID.
requirements.condition: When identifying a stream within a connection
requirements.required_behavior: Use a numeric stream ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The representation used to identify streams within a connection can be inspected or exercised.

requirements.quote: A stream ID is a 62-bit integer (0 to 2^62-1)
requirements.condition: For every stream ID
requirements.required_behavior: Represent a value in the inclusive range 0 through 2^62-1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a negative value or a value greater than 2^62-1 as a stream ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and out-of-range stream ID values can be supplied and their handling observed.

requirements.quote: A stream ID is a 62-bit integer (0 to 2^62-1) that is unique for all streams on a connection.
requirements.condition: For streams within the same connection
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a stream ID that is unique among all streams on that connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign the same stream ID to multiple streams on one connection.
requirements.why_checkable: All stream identifiers created on one connection can be compared for uniqueness.

requirements.quote: Stream IDs are encoded as variable-length integers; see Section 16.
requirements.condition: When encoding a stream ID
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the stream ID as a variable-length integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The wire encoding of stream IDs can be inspected to determine whether it uses the variable-length integer representation.

requirements.quote: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a stream ID within a connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint assigns or uses stream IDs during a connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse any stream ID previously used within that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection trace can detect any repeated use of a stream ID after its initial use.

requirements.quote: The least significant bit (0x01) of the stream ID identifies the initiator of the stream.
requirements.condition: When determining or encoding the initiator of a stream
requirements.required_behavior: Use the stream ID's least significant bit as the initiator indicator.
requirements.why_checkable: The initiator associated with a stream can be compared with bit 0 of its stream ID.

requirements.quote: Client-initiated streams have even-numbered stream IDs (with the bit set to 0)
requirements.condition: When a stream is initiated by the client
requirements.required_behavior: Use an even-numbered stream ID whose least significant bit is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign an odd-numbered stream ID to a client-initiated stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Client-created stream IDs can be checked for parity and bit 0.

requirements.quote: server-initiated streams have odd-numbered stream IDs (with the bit set to 1).
requirements.condition: When a stream is initiated by the server
requirements.required_behavior: Use an odd-numbered stream ID whose least significant bit is 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign an even-numbered stream ID to a server-initiated stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Server-created stream IDs can be checked for parity and bit 0.

requirements.quote: The second least significant bit (0x02) of the stream ID distinguishes between bidirectional streams (with the bit set to 0) and unidirectional streams (with the bit set to 1).
requirements.condition: When determining or encoding stream directionality
requirements.required_behavior: Use the stream ID's second least significant bit as the directionality indicator.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream's directionality can be compared with bit 1 of its stream ID.

requirements.quote: bidirectional streams (with the bit set to 0)
requirements.condition: When a stream is bidirectional
requirements.required_behavior: Set the stream ID's second least significant bit to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set the stream ID's second least significant bit to 1 for a bidirectional stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 1 of every bidirectional stream ID can be inspected.

requirements.quote: unidirectional streams (with the bit set to 1).
requirements.condition: When a stream is unidirectional
requirements.required_behavior: Set the stream ID's second least significant bit to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set the stream ID's second least significant bit to 0 for a unidirectional stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit 1 of every unidirectional stream ID can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The two least significant bits from a stream ID therefore identify a stream as one of four types
requirements.condition: When classifying a stream by its stream ID
requirements.required_behavior: Determine one of four stream types from the two least significant bits.
requirements.why_checkable: All four two-bit combinations can be tested against the implementation's stream classification.

requirements.quote: | 0x00 | Client-Initiated, Bidirectional |
requirements.condition: When the two least significant stream ID bits are 0x00
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the stream as client-initiated and bidirectional.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream ID ending in binary 00 can be supplied and its classification observed.

requirements.quote: | 0x01 | Server-Initiated, Bidirectional |
requirements.condition: When the two least significant stream ID bits are 0x01
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the stream as server-initiated and bidirectional.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream ID ending in binary 01 can be supplied and its classification observed.

requirements.quote: | 0x02 | Client-Initiated, Unidirectional |
requirements.condition: When the two least significant stream ID bits are 0x02
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the stream as client-initiated and unidirectional.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream ID ending in binary 10 can be supplied and its classification observed.

requirements.quote: | 0x03 | Server-Initiated, Unidirectional |
requirements.condition: When the two least significant stream ID bits are 0x03
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the stream as server-initiated and unidirectional.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream ID ending in binary 11 can be supplied and its classification observed.

requirements.quote: The stream space for each type begins at the minimum value (0x00 through 0x03, respectively)
requirements.condition: When opening the first stream in each stream type's stream space
requirements.required_behavior: Begin the client-initiated bidirectional space at 0x00, server-initiated bidirectional space at 0x01, client-initiated unidirectional space at 0x02, and server-initiated unidirectional space at 0x03.
requirements.why_checkable: The first stream ID produced for each of the four types can be compared with its specified minimum.

requirements.quote: successive streams of each type are created with numerically increasing stream IDs.
requirements.condition: When creating successive streams of the same type
requirements.required_behavior: Use numerically increasing stream IDs.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not create a successive stream of a type with a stream ID lower than an earlier stream ID of that type.
requirements.why_checkable: The sequence of IDs used for streams of each type can be recorded and checked for numerical increase.

requirements.quote: A stream ID that is used out of order results in all streams of that type with lower- numbered stream IDs also being opened.
requirements.condition: When a stream ID is used out of order
requirements.required_behavior: Treat all lower-numbered stream IDs of the same stream type as opened.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave a lower-numbered stream of that type unopened.
requirements.why_checkable: After an out-of-order stream ID is used, the implementation's state for every lower-numbered stream of the same type can be inspected.
